# Spar 0.7.0

**Spar 0.7 rebuilds the coach as one agent. The phase controller that walked
every turn through fixed stages is gone. The coach now runs as a plain loop
with one stable set of tools and one prompt, keeps a notebook about you, and
sets, edits and follows up on challenges when it judges they are needed.**

## One coach, one loop

- **No more stages.** The coach sees the same tools for the whole session and
  decides what comes next. Spar still owns stopping, steering, provider
  timeouts, context overflow and the final verdict on every run.
- **The coach writes a brief, a builder writes the challenge.** `set_challenge`
  takes an aim, a stretch, a difficulty and a task. A separate builder turn
  turns that into the statement, starter, reference and tests, using the same
  starters your Track already uses. Spar compiles and validates the result, and
  repairs it in the same call when validation fails. The builder now checks that
  a statement's definitions produce the numbers the reference computes, so a
  challenge can't define height in edges and count it in nodes.
- **Small changes stay small.** `edit_challenge` applies exact find-and-replace
  edits to the open challenge: a reworded sentence, an added figure, a fixed
  test. Only what the edit could break is re-checked. A starter edit reaches your
  file only if you haven't changed that part, and the thread shows each edit as
  a word-level diff.
- **Gaps are practised on a new problem.** When a solution has already been
  shown, the coach moves the gap to a different problem instead of re-setting
  the one you solved.
- **Prompt caching.** Every model call sends a stable cache key, so long
  sessions stop re-sending the same 15–33k tokens uncached on every step.

## The coach's notebook

- **A notebook per Track, kept by the coach.** It records what it learned about
  you and what it decided, and it leads the context of every turn. Edits are
  exact find-and-replace changes, not rewrites.
- **You can read and edit it.** Open it from the Track header to view it, change
  it, or browse its history. Notebook and ability updates show in the thread as
  a card with a diff against the previous version.

## Figures

- **Every figure can be annotated.** Tones, labels, removed items, edge tones and
  captions work on every figure, and every key is checked against the structure,
  so a highlight can't point at something that isn't there.
- **Graphs are laid out by Graphviz**, top to bottom, with display names, boxes,
  self-loops and Graphviz's edge routes.
- **Richer figures.** Grids become DP tables with headers and arrows. Arrays get
  ranges, arcs and bars. Linked lists get pointers, reversal, cuts and extra
  links. New stack, interval, table and column figures.
- **Broken figures don't reach you.** A lesson with an invalid figure is
  refused, and a reply containing one goes back to the coach once to fix it.

## Activity

- **A practice calendar in Settings.** The new Activity page shows a year of
  days, shaded by how much you solved, with a lighter shade for days you worked
  but didn't solve anything. You can filter it to Spar, LeetCode or Codeforces.
  Below the calendar are your sources, your rhythm, your streak and everything
  you've solved. Only your own work counts.
- **The concept sheet is reworked.** Your standing shows as a word, the pass
  count behind it and a bar, with the volume in plain numbers, so "strong
  across 2" and "strong across 40" look different. Abilities are listed one per
  line, and a challenge set more than once shows as one row with a count.

## The window

- **Settings uses the app's sidebar** rather than opening a second one next to
  it, with "Back to app" as the first row.
- **Sessions remember where you were.** Leaving a session and coming back
  returns you to the Problem or Chat tab you left, at the same scroll position,
  with your open folds still open.
- **The sidebar is narrower and cheaper to drag.** It opens at 290px and is
  capped at 340px or a quarter of the window. Dragging it or a pane divider no
  longer re-renders the whole app on every pixel, and a drag always ends when
  you let go, wherever the pointer is.

## Fixes

- A run whose cases all pass but whose process exits with an error now shows
  Runtime Error with the raw output, instead of "Solved. Accepted" while Spar
  recorded a failure. The case count no longer shows more passes than cases.
- A new challenge in the same session now replaces the workspace. A previous
  challenge's test file used to stay behind and fail every submission.
- An accepted review of an attempt whose last submission passed every case and
  failed only on the exit code now completes the attempt.
- The chat opens at the latest message again, rather than partway up while
  code, maths and figures finish drawing.

## Removed

The rule-based learning engine that came before the coach is gone:

- **Baseline calibration.** The coach now places a new learner from their
  answers and a first challenge, and writes it in the notebook. Old baseline
  sessions stay hidden from lists.
- **Training mode** on Home, which the coach never read.
- **Today's decisions.** Home now shows the challenge the coach last set and the
  ability it targets. The old decisions table is dropped when the app opens.
- **The Learning Engine settings page.**

Abilities, evidence, patterns, notices, ratings and spaced review are
unchanged.

## Downloads

| Your machine | File |
| --- | --- |
| Mac, Apple silicon | `Spar-0.7.0-arm64.dmg` |
| Mac, Intel | `Spar-0.7.0.dmg` |
| Windows | `Spar-0.7.0-x64.exe` |
| Linux | `Spar-0.7.0-x86_64.AppImage` or `Spar-0.7.0-amd64.deb` |

## Known limits

- This open distribution is unsigned. macOS Gatekeeper or Windows SmartScreen
  may ask you to approve the first launch, and those platforms may require a
  manual installer step for an update.
- Linux AppImage installations can self-update when the runtime supports it;
  `.deb` installations stay managed by the system package manager.
